neutral_facts.value: The incident occurred at night in a village when the accused, who were armed with weapons, attacked two deceased individuals and two injured witnesses. The accused were involved in a confrontation, and the deceased were not armed. The prosecution presented evidence including statements from injured witnesses, medical reports detailing the injuries sustained by both the deceased and the accused, and a post-mortem report confirming stab wounds on the deceased. The accused claimed they were acting in self-defense, but the court found no evidence to support this claim. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 IPC for causing the deaths of the deceased.

defence_argument.value: The appellants have lodged cross First Information Report. They argue that the deceased and their accomplices, 9 in number, were the aggressors. The injuries have been inflicted on both the appellants. Such injuries have been proved by PW-10, Dr. Nikhilkumar Buch. The appellants have received grievous injuries, while protecting the possession of their land, thus, they have acted in their right of private defence. They also argue that the occurrence has taken place at the spur of the moment without any pre-meditation and that the appellants are not taken any advantage or acted in a cruel or unusual manner.

legal_principle_applied.value: The right of private defence is to protect the person and the property. In such right, the person cannot cause more harm than what is necessary for the protection of the person and the property. The right of private defence is not available when the alleged assailants are unarmed.
